title: Match a training specification
scenario: Arelvon Tube Lab has 24 invented tensile samples. Match each Product_code to the Specs sheet; a blank or unlisted code must return Missing, and repeated sample records remain separate. These limits are fictitious training rules, not a published standard.

lesson.intro: A lookup connects records by an explicit key. Match exact product codes rather than assuming that sample and specification rows are in the same order.

functions.name: XLOOKUP
functions.purpose: Find a key and return its corresponding value.
functions.arguments: Supply the key, aligned key and return ranges, optional missing label, match mode (0 exact, -1 next smaller, 1 next larger), and search direction (1 first, -1 last).
functions.mistake: Exact is the default. A first match does not aggregate duplicates. Binary search requires correctly sorted keys.

functions.name: INDEX
functions.purpose: Return the value at a row and column position.
functions.arguments: array contains values; row_num selects its row and optional column_num selects its column.
functions.useCase: Select an item in a specification matrix.
functions.mistake: Row positions are relative to the selected array, not worksheet row numbers.

lesson.combine: Reuse IF for a strength decision and ROUND when displaying a strength-to-limit ratio. A valid zero and a missing key are different; protect missing matches before doing arithmetic.

tasks.prompt: Look up Yield_min_MPa for the first sample’s Product_code.
Return the second Specs row’s Yield_min_MPa by its position within the four-row specification array.
For the first six samples, return Pass if Yield_MPa is at least the matched minimum, Hold if below it, or Missing if the product key is blank/unlisted. Keep dataset order.
For the first sample, calculate Yield_MPa divided by its matched minimum, rounded to three decimals.

bonus.prompt: Return the final specification row’s Product_code using its array position.
